note: Settlements decided by a researcher reading the name against the path and collection it is filed under, each with a Wikidata item, a point, the pages that say so and a sentence. Merged by scripts/merge-unplaced-decisions.py after the point was checked against the country outline. A name that was not established is simply not here.
source: Wikidata (CC0) and Wikipedia, as cited per row

placed.why: Wikidata Q38022 is the independent city of St. Louis, Missouri, and the filing sits at [County] level in a Missouri probate collection, matching the city's county-equivalent status.
Wikipedia describes the Minster Church of St Nicholas as the parish church of Great Yarmouth, Norfolk, and the collection is Norfolk parish registers.

Wikipedia/Wikidata give Manila as the city, and FamilySearch's Manila civil registration collection is sourced from the City of Manila Civil Registrar; 'Municipal' is the FamilySearch label for that registry and no other Manila exists in the Philippines (weak: no page uses the exact label).
Wikidata Q60554140 is Dunaghy civil parish in County Antrim and townlands.ie lists it in Kilconway barony; the path is Antrim > Dunaghy at [Parish] level in Ireland census/valuation collections.

Wikipedia gives 'St. Andrews East' as the old English name of its post office (Saint-André-Est), and it has an Anglican Christ Church (1819-21) and a Church of Scotland Presbyterian church; I found no source for the Congregational church, so this rests on Anglican and Presbyterian agreement.
'Wien (alle Bezirke)' means Vienna, all districts; the collection 'Austria, Vienna, Jewish Registers' agrees; the point is Wikipedia/Wikidata's for the city.

placed.gazetteer: Higashinakatomi (東中富), Aizumi, Itano District, Tokushima
placed.why: ja.wikipedia lists 東中富村 of Itano-gun among six villages merged into 藍園村 in 1889, and 東中富 is today an ōaza of 藍住町; no Wikidata item of its own exists, so the point and QID are the town of Aizumi's (approximate, same town).

placed.n: Aizumi-chō Higashinakatomi 藍住町東中富
placed.gazetteer: Higashinakatomi (東中富), Aizumi, Itano District, Tokushima
placed.why: ja.wikipedia lists 東中富 (ひがしなかとみ) as an ōaza of 藍住町, Itano-gun, Tokushima, the modern name of 東中富村 (same 236 volumes as the Awa no kuni entry); point and QID are the town of Aizumi's, not the ōaza's own.
Parish entry 'České Budějovice: České Budějovice' in the Southern Bohemia Třeboň Archive church books; České Budějovice is the South Bohemian city on Wikipedia/Wikidata.

ru Wikipedia Смолдеярово documents a stone Kazan-Bogoroditskaya church (1902-1905) there; the Nashi Predki church page gives Смолдиярово as a variant of the village in Laishevsky uezd, Kazan Governorate; the Tatarstan collection family agrees (no path was supplied in the batch).

The name is the town Вышний Волочёк (Wikidata ru alias Вышний Волочек) in the former Tver Governorate; the hyphenated form is the same name; no other town of the name exists. FamilySearch gave no path or collection for this name, so only the name itself agrees.
ru Wikipedia: the town Лаишево was named Лаишев until 1926 and has a Sofiysky cathedral; Wikidata ru alias Лаишев; the path is Laishev uezd and the collection is Russia, Tatarstan.

ru Wikipedia: Novye Shimkusy was the centre of Novoshimkusskaya volost, Tetyushsky uezd, Kazan Governorate (1797-1920) and has a Church of the Nativity of Christ (Христорождественская); the path lists Тетюши, so the uezd agrees; Новыя is the pre-1918 spelling of Новые; village is in Chuvashia today.

Swedish Wikipedia's S:t Johannes församling page is reached by the redirect 'Johannes församling, Stockholm' and the collection is 'Sweden, Stockholm, Church Records'; the parish was split from Jakob och Johannes in 1907, which fits the 'för Jakob' series in the path, but older books may belong to Jakob och Johannes församling (Q54006791, about 1 km away at 59.3304, 18.0706).

Swedish Wikipedia states the parish bore the names Kungsholms and Ulrika Eleonora församling (the latter from 1688, the two used together), seated in Kungsholms kyrka in Stockholm, matching the Stockholm church-records collection.

placed.gazetteer: Sagrario Metropolitano, Mexico City (parish of the Metropolitan Cathedral)
placed.why: Wikipedia places the Sagrario Metropolitano immediately to the right of the cathedral, where parishioners are registered; the Sagrario has no item of its own and 'Sagrario Metropolitano' redirects to the cathedral item Q610961, whose P625 is used (the buildings are adjacent). Cathedral is the Assumption cathedral, matching 'Asunción'.

placed.n: Santa Cruz y Soledad (Centro-Barrio la Soledad)
placed.gazetteer: Church of Santa Cruz y La Soledad (La Merced, Mexico City)
placed.why: Wikipedia: the church is officially the Church of Santa Cruz y La Soledad, in the La Merced area of central Mexico City; infobox coordinates 19.4317,-99.1230 equal Wikidata P625; matches 'Mexico, Distrito Federal' collection and the 'Soledad' barrio.

placed.gazetteer: Cathedral of Sts. Philip and James, Azcapotzalco
placed.why: es.wikipedia 'Catedral de Azcapotzalco' (infobox: Catedral de los Santos Apóstoles Felipe y Santiago) says it was the parish until its 2019 consecration as a cathedral; coordinates 19.48056,-99.18544 equal Wikidata P625.
Wikipedia: national cemetery in Asunción established 1842 (matches the collection 'Paraguay, Asunción, Cemetery Records, 1842-2012'); infobox 25.2927S 57.5894W equals Wikidata P625.
The string names Salisbury, filed under Zimbabwe in 'Zimbabwe Death Notices, 1904-1976'; Salisbury is the pre-1982 name of Harare (Wikipedia). The point is the city's, not the Market Square's own.

Wikipedia: 'It retained the name Salisbury until 1982 when it was renamed Harare'; Wikidata aliases 'Salisbury, Rhodesia' and 'Salisbury, Zimbabwe'. Applies to the ZW-filed books (Zimbabwe Death Notices, 1904-1976); the other paths under the same string (Wiltshire, Essex MA) belong to different Salisburys and should not be drawn here.

placed.gazetteer: San Bernardino de Siena Church, Xochimilco
placed.why: Wikipedia: San Bernardino de Siena Church is the parish church of the Xochimilco borough of Mexico City (now cathedral of the Diocese of Xochimilco); spelling 'Sena' is a variant of 'Siena'.

The Corpi Santi di Cremona were the suburban farms/villages outside Cremona's walls, a separate comune 1757-1871 and then annexed to the city, so "Cremona e Corpi Santi" is the city with its suburb belt; the collection is Cremona.
it.wikipedia: Sant'Elena Sannita (già Cameli), called Cameli until 1896; province of Isernia agrees with the path.
it.wikipedia on Jelsi lists Ielsi as the name used under the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies; Campobasso (Molise) collection agrees.
The it.wikipedia article is titled Pettoranello del Molise and its infobox names the comune "Pettoranello di Molise"; Isernia province agrees.
San Vincenzo al Volturno was a separate comune merged in 1928 with Castellone al Volturno to form Castel San Vincenzo (Isernia); the point is the successor comune, not the village itself.
it.wikipedia: Castri di Lecce arose from the union of the two casali Castrifrancone and Castriguarino (united in the 1890s); the point is the merged comune, Lecce province agrees.
it.wikipedia: Minturno was known as Traetto until the 19th century and took back its old name on 13 July 1879; it was in Terra di Lavoro (Caserta) and is now in Latina, matching the path.
The it.wikipedia disambiguation page for Sicignano lists only Sicignano degli Alburni as a place, and its article uses Sicignano for the comune in the Salerno district under the Two Sicilies.
Samo was named Precacore until 1911 (it.wikipedia article and the Calabria comune-changes list: Precacore RC 1911 renamed Samo); Reggio Calabria collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: Satriano di Lucania was called Pietrafesa until 1887; the Pietrafesa disambiguation page says the same; Potenza (Basilicata) agrees.
it.wikipedia: the comune was called Salvia until renamed Savoia di Lucania in 1879; Potenza collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: the boroughs Mola and Castellone were fused into one comune in 1820 which took the name Formia in 1862; it was in Terra di Lavoro (Caserta) and is now in Latina, matching the path.
it.wikipedia: Specchia (Lecce) was called Specchia De' Preti until 1873; the form with the particle dropped is the same name and no other Specchia Preti turned up; Lecce collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: in 1862 the comune changed its name from Coreno to Coreno Ausonio; it belonged to Terra di Lavoro (Caserta) until 1927 and is now in Frosinone, matching the path.
Calabria comune-changes list: Campo RC was renamed Campo di Calabria in 1864 and Campo Calabro in 1950; Reggio Calabria collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: Bellantone is a frazione contiguous to the centre of Laureana di Borrello (Reggio Calabria); no coordinate of its own found, so the point is the comune centre.
Rivarolo Fuori was renamed Rivarolo Mantovano in 1907 (it.wikipedia; Lombardy comune-changes list); Mantova collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: Noepoli was called Noja until 1863 (Noia is the same spelling with i for j); Potenza collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: Sinopoli Superiore is the municipal seat (sede comunale) of the comune of Sinopoli in the Reggio Calabria area; the collection agrees.
en.wikipedia: Roccapipirozzi (also written Rocca Pipirozzi) is a frazione of Sesto Campano in the province of Isernia; point from its infobox.
The comune Gerre de' Caprioli is in the province of Cremona, matching the collection.
Lombardy comune-changes list: San Daniele CR became San Daniele Ripa Po in 1867 and San Daniele Po in 1955; Cremona collection agrees.
Sicily comune-changes list: Mazara TP was renamed Mazara del Vallo in 1863; the Mazara disambiguation page points to it; Trapani collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: Castri di Lecce arose from the union of the two casali Castrifrancone and Castriguarino; the point is the merged comune, Lecce province agrees.
it.wikipedia: Nocera Corpo was one of the comuni born in 1806 from the split of Nocera dei Pagani, covering the present Nocera Superiore; the point is its successor comune (Salerno).
Wikidata has a settlement Carifi-Torello-Priscoli located in Mercato San Severino (Salerno); the article lists Torello and Carifi as adjacent villages there. The label adds Priscoli.
Cà de' Stefani CR was a comune until 1927, when it was merged into Vescovato; it remains a frazione in Cremona province, matching the collection.
Montoro Inferiore was a comune (dissolved in 2013, now Montoro, Avellino); under the Two Sicilies it lay in the Principato Citra intendenza, i.e. Salerno province, matching the Salerno collection.
it.wikipedia: Salento was called Sala di Gioi until 1863; Salerno collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: Alezio was called Villapicciotti (Villa Picciotti) until 1873; Lecce province agrees.
"Amalfi e frazioni" is the comune of Amalfi together with its hamlets (e.g. Pogerola); the collection is Salerno civil registration, and Amalfi is in the province of Salerno.

Wikipedia says the town grew around the harbour mole (molo) of Girgenti, was called Molo di Girgenti, got autonomy in 1853 and was renamed Porto Empedocle in 1863; the 1820-1865 Agrigento collection fits that period.

The spelling "Roccalbenga (GR)" is used for a Grosseto-province place in a source page, and Roccalbegna is the only such comune in the province of Grosseto, matching the Grosseto collection; the spelling is a variant (not on the Roccalbegna page itself).

Wikipedia: Gallico has a hilly part, Gallico Superiore, and a coastal one; the Bourbon Distretto di Reggio lists Gallico Superiore as a comune with the village Gallico Inferiore. Point is an OpenStreetMap place way for Gallico Superiore (Wikidata item Q3757804 has no coordinate on its own for the hilly part).
Wikipedia has the comune San Pietro in Gu in the province of Padova; Italian sources also write it with the accent (Gù), and the collection is Padova.
The Wikipedia page for San Pier Niceto says the centre was originally called "San Pier Monforte" until it was renamed (listed as changing name in 1873); the collection is Messina 1820-1865.

The Distretto di Reggio lists Gallico Inferiore as a village of Gallico Superiore, and the Grande Reggio page describes it as the lower part along the sea; the point is the Wikipedia infobox point for Gallico (whole quartiere) as Gallico Inferiore has no own coordinate.
Wikipedia has Barberino Val d'Elsa in the metropolitan city of Firenze (a comune until 2019), matching the Firenze path in the Toscana collection.

placed.gazetteer: Gallina (formerly Sant'Agata in Gallina), Reggio Calabria
placed.why: Gallina was founded in 1783 as the "new city of Sant'Agata in Gallina" and the Distretto di Reggio lists the comune Sant'Agata in Gallina; the point is the OpenStreetMap village node for Gallina (Wikipedia page has no coordinate).
Wikipedia: San Giuliano del Sannio was "San Giuliano di Sepino" until 1863; province of Campobasso agrees with the collection 1809-1918.

Wikipedia: Moltedo was once split into the borgate Moltedo Superiore and Moltedo Inferiore, listed as separate comuni in the Porto Maurizio circondario; Imperia collection agrees. Point is the frazione Moltedo as a whole.

Wikipedia has Cannavò as a quartiere of Reggio Calabria and the Distretto di Reggio lists it as a village of Cataforio; point is the OpenStreetMap residential area for Cannavò (the Wikipedia item has no coordinate).
Wikipedia states the territory was called "San Bartolomeo del Cervo" until the later renaming, and Wikidata lists it as an alias; province of Imperia agrees.
Wikipedia: Villa Littorio was called Fogna until 1930, an autonomous village until 1875, now a frazione of Laurino in Salerno province, matching the Salerno collection.

Wikipedia: Invorio was formed in 1928 from the suppressed comune of Invorio Superiore joined to Invorio Inferiore; path is Novara. Point is the OpenStreetMap village node (Wikidata item has no coordinate).

Wikipedia: Divaccia (Divača) hosts the San Canziano (Škocjan) caves on the Timavo; the collection is Trieste 1924-1944 and the path files it under Slovenia. "Grotte del Timavo" is treated as the added descriptor; Wikidata alias lists "Divaccia San Canziano".
Wikipedia: Ogliara is a località of the comune of Salerno, and the Salerno diocese pages treat Ogliara as a forania; point is the OpenStreetMap hamlet node (Wikidata item has no coordinate).
"Camerota e frazioni" is the comune of Camerota (with Marina di Camerota etc.); the collection is Salerno civil registration and Camerota is in the province of Salerno.

placed.n: Rovereto: Parrochia di San Marco Evangelista
placed.why: Wikipedia lists the Chiesa arcipretale di San Marco in Rovereto (Trentino); the parish book collection is the Diocese of Trento, so the point is the town of Rovereto.
Italian Wikipedia gives San Martino dall'Argine as a comune of the province of Mantua, matching the Mantova civil registration collection.

it.wikipedia (Distretto di Vallo) lists Ascea 'con i casali di Catona e Mandia', and the Ascea page lists Catona and Mandia as its frazioni; the Salerno collection agrees. Point is the successor comune Ascea.

it.wikipedia lists Arcara and Casaburi-Rotolo among the frazioni of Cava de' Tirreni (province of Salerno, matching the collection); the joint name is not itself stated, so the point is the successor comune.
it.wikipedia (Gussago) states that under the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy the municipality was renamed 'Gussago con Ronco'; Ronco is a frazione of Gussago; Brescia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia names Monteghirfo as a frazione of Favale di Malvaro (administratively shared with Lorsica) in the Genoa area, matching the Genova collection; the point is the Wikidata item's own P625.

it.wikipedia (Bagnolo Mella) lists the Napoleonic-era municipality 'Azzano con Pontegatello'; Wikidata Q18476192 places the village Pontegatello in Azzano Mella (Brescia), which is the only comune that fits the Brescia collection. Point is Azzano Mella.

Sale Marasino is the Brescia comune on the east shore of Lake Iseo that joins the two names Sale and Marasino; the Brescia collection agrees. The joint form 'Sale con Marasino' is the older municipal style used for Brescia comuni (cf. Gussago con Ronco).
it.wikipedia (Sermide e Felonica) names Quatrelle as a former parish-frazione of that Mantua comune; Wikidata has the same place as 'Quattrelle' in Sermide e Felonica.
it.wikipedia states that in 1927 the comuni of Inzino and Magno were added to Gardone Val Trompia and are now frazioni; Brescia collection agrees. Point is Inzino's own P625.
it.wikipedia (Scafati) describes San Pietro (with the abbey of Santa Maria di Realvalle) as a locality in the comune of Scafati, Salerno; the point is the comune's, not the locality's.
it.wikipedia (Bovegno) says the comune absorbed the tiny comune of Magno in 1339 and that Magno has the church of San Lorenzo; Brescia collection agrees.
Monastier di Treviso is the Treviso comune whose name is 'Monastier' in Veneto dialect and in the page text, matching the Treviso 1806-1815 collection.
it.wikipedia (Provaglio d'Iseo) lists Provezze and Fantecolo as the frazioni of the comune and speaks of the earlier separate comune of Provezze; Brescia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia (Monticelli d'Oglio) says it was an autonomous comune until 1842 and links Villanuova with it; Brescia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia says Montebello took the name 'Fossato di Calabria Ultra I' from 1862-64 until 1890 in the list of renamed comuni; Reggio Calabria collection (1784-1943) agrees.
it.wikipedia lists Alessia and Marini among the frazioni of Cava de' Tirreni (province of Salerno, as in the collection); the joint name is not itself stated, so the point is the successor comune.
it.wikipedia (Bagnolo Mella) lists the Napoleonic-era municipality 'Flero con Coller'; Flero is the only comune of that name in Brescia province, matching the collection.

it.wikipedia (Cordignano) says the village was long called San Cassiano del Meschio (dialect San Cassan del Mesch); 'Mesco' is the same river name as spelled in the register; Treviso collection agrees.
it.wikipedia (Pederobba) says the municipal seat is the frazione Onigo and names Covolo as another of its localities, in Treviso province as in the collection; the point is the successor comune.
it.wikipedia (Cappella Maggiore) describes the parish of Anzano within the comune, in Treviso province as in the collection; the point is the comune's.
it.wikipedia (Rubano) names Bosco di Rubano as one of its three frazioni; Padova collection agrees. The point is the comune's, not the frazione's (no Wikidata item found for the frazione).
it.wikipedia (Mogliano Veneto) names Zerman and Bonisiolo as its frazioni, in Treviso province as in the collection; the point is the successor comune.

placed.n: Fiera di Primiero: Parrochia di Santa Maria Assunta
placed.why: The path names the parish of Fiera di Primiero in the Diocese of Trento; it.wikipedia gives Fiera di Primiero as the former comune and administrative seat of Primiero San Martino di Castrozza.
it.wikipedia (Moltedo) says the village was once split into the borgate Moltedo Superiore and Moltedo Inferiore and was a comune until 1923 (Imperia); the point is Moltedo's own P625.
it.wikipedia (Treviso) lists Canizzano and Sant'Angelo as the western quarters of the city, matching the Treviso collection; the point is the city's.
it.wikipedia (Volpago del Montello) describes Volpago and Selva as the two centres of the comune, in Treviso province as in the collection.
it.wikipedia's Buzzoletto disambiguation says Buzzoletto is a frazione of Viadana in the province of Mantua (the other Buzzolettos are cascine near Novara); the Mantova collection decides.
Wikidata places Boscalto (Q18500915) in Resana (Q46494), a Treviso comune, matching the collection; the point is Resana's.
it.wikipedia says the unit was founded in 1784 as Quattroville and renamed Virgilio in 1883 (Wikidata alias Quattroville); the Mantova collection agrees.

it.wikipedia says Moltedo was split into the hamlets Moltedo Superiore and Moltedo Inferiore and was an autonomous comune before joining Imperia in 1923; point is the whole village of Moltedo (Inferiore is one half), Imperia collection agrees.

it.wikipedia lists Frontignano as a frazione of Barbariga (comune of Frontignano aggregated to Barbariga by decree of 1927, effective 1928); the combined name is not itself quoted, point is Barbariga.

it.wikipedia lists Priscoli (with the locality San Martino) among the 23 frazioni of Mercato San Severino, Salerno, matching the Salerno collection; no other Priscoli in Salerno was found; the frazione has no Wikidata item found, so the point is the comune's.
it.wikipedia lists Pievedizio as the frazione of Mairano (Brescia); the combined name is not itself quoted, point is Mairano.
it.wikipedia lists Sicilì as the only frazione of Morigerati (Salerno) and the Distretto di Sala page names Morigerati 'con il casale di Sicilì'.

Single-t spelling of Quattroville, the pre-1883 name of Virgilio per it.wikipedia and Wikidata alias; the exact spelling Quatroville is not itself attested in a page I opened, but it is the same Mantova collection and the only such place.
it.wikipedia lists Marina among Vietri sul Mare's frazioni and calls it the seaside district; point is the comune's.

placed.n: Siviano con Carzano, Novale e Monte d'Isola
placed.why: it.wikipedia names Siviano (seat), Carzano and Novale as the localities of Monte Isola (Brescia, Lake Iseo).
it.wikipedia lists Cortine among the frazioni of Nave (Brescia).
it.wikipedia: Borgonato was an independent comune until 1928, now in Corte Franca; Monterotondo (a locality of Passirano) borders it; the combined name is not itself quoted, point is Borgonato.
it.wikipedia lists Bargnano and Meano as frazioni of Corzano (Brescia).
it.wikipedia calls Borgo Poncarale the only frazione of Poncarale (Brescia).
it.wikipedia says the comune arose from annexing Cizzago to Comezzano; Marrochina is not mentioned there, so only Cizzago is evidenced; point is the successor comune.

placed.n: Pergine Valsugana: Parrochia di Natività Beata Vergine Maria
placed.why: it.wikipedia names the pieve church of the Natività di Maria at Pergine Valsugana, matching the Diocesi di Trento collection.
it.wikipedia lists Castelli as a frazione of Monfumo (Treviso).
it.wikipedia lists Raito and Albori as frazioni of Vietri sul Mare (Salerno); point is the comune's.
it.wikipedia lists Solighetto as a frazione of Pieve di Soligo (Treviso).

placed.n: Borgo Valsugana: Parrochia di Natività di Maria Santissima
placed.why: it.wikipedia names the Chiesa arcipretale della Natività di Maria at Borgo Valsugana, matching the Diocesi di Trento collection.
it.wikipedia lists Carzago Riviera as a frazione of Calvagese della Riviera (Brescia); Arzaga was not found in any page I opened, so only Carzago is evidenced.
it.wikipedia states the comune of Silea was called Melma until 1935; the Treviso collections (1806-1815 and 1871-1941) agree.
it.wikipedia: Campalto was a frazione of the comune of Favaro from 1819 to 1926, then merged into Venice; 'e frazioni' is not quoted; Venezia path agrees.
it.wikipedia says the comune was named Levico until 1969 and has the church of the Santissimo Redentore (1872-77), matching the Diocesi di Trento collection.
it.wikipedia's Peraga disambiguation lists only Peraga (Vigonza), a frazione in Padova province, matching the Padova collection.

Annone Veneto is the only Annone in the Venezia area; it.wikipedia puts it in the Città metropolitana di Venezia (in 1806-17 it fell under Pordenone/San Vito districts per the page, so the period fit is only indirect).
it.wikipedia says Granze became a municipality in 1914 by separating from Vescovana and borders it (Padova); the exact name 'Granze di Vescovana' is not quoted.

it.wikipedia lists Sant'Angelo as a frazione of Santa Maria di Sala, which belonged to the province of Padova until 1853, fitting the Padova collection; the frazione has no item found, so the point is the comune's.
it.wikipedia says the territory was split in the Cisalpine period into Cavarzere Destro, San Giuseppe and Rottanova; Cavarzere Destro is part of today's Cavarzere (Venezia).
it.wikipedia: the centre was originally called Mulo and renamed Villa Poma in 1868; Mantova collection agrees.
it.wikipedia lists Crespignaga and Coste as frazioni of Maser (Treviso).
it.wikipedia lists Lovadina and Visnadello as the frazioni of Spresiano (Treviso).
it.wikipedia: Castelminio, a frazione of Resana, was formerly called Brusaporco.

it.wikipedia says Cataforio lay under the fortified Motta Sant'Agata (its suburb until 1783) on the Torrente Sant'Agata, so the paired name points to Cataforio; Reggio Calabria collection agrees (point is Cataforio's own, Sant'Agata being ~1 km away).
it.wikipedia lists Fimiani as a frazione of Castel San Giorgio (province of Salerno) and Wikidata has an item for it; no other Fimiani frazione found in Salerno.

placed.n: Moltedo Superiore (Parrocchia di San Bernardo Abate)
placed.why: it.wikipedia says Moltedo was split into the borgate Moltedo Superiore and Inferiore, its parish church is San Bernardo, and it was a comune until 1923 (Imperia); the Imperia collection agrees.

it.wikipedia: Alì Terme was the coastal frazione of Alì, a comune from 1911 as Alì Marina (renamed Alì Terme 1954); Messina collection agrees; note the register name predates the 1911 comune (Wikidata alias Alì Marina).
it.wikipedia says the comune name is made of the two localities Cavallino and Treporti, which until 1999 were part of Venice; Venezia 1806-1817 collection agrees.
it.wikipedia states the centre was anciently called Bagno a Corsena, recorded by ISTAT as the earlier name of Bagni di Lucca; Lucca collection agrees.

it.wikipedia (Pedergnaga) says the territory was merged into Oriano, which was renamed Oriano con Pedergnaga e Trignano (1927), later Pedergnaga Oriano and, from 1964, San Paolo (BS); point is Oriano's own, the three places lie within about 1 km.
it.wikipedia lists Fontane as a frazione of Villorba and says Villorba and Fontane were Napoleonic municipalities later in the one comune; Treviso collections agree.
it.wikipedia (Capriano del Colle) says territory was assigned to Capriano to form the comune of Capriano con Movico; Brescia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia says Gambara's only frazione is Corvione; Brescia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia explains the bipartite name Torbole Casaglia (Casaglia = old Casaglio form) as two settlements, Torbole and Casaglia, in the one comune; Brescia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia states the comune was called Comune di Isorella con San Nazzaro until the end of the 1800s.
it.wikipedia infobox gives Brandico frazioni Castelgonelle and Ognato, and the Bagnolo Mella page lists the Napoleonic municipality Brandico con Ognato e Castelgonelle; Brescia collection agrees.
Wikidata gives the alias Padernello con Mottella for Padernello, and it.wikipedia says Motella formed a comune with Padernello in 1816-1859; both lie in Borgo San Giacomo, Brescia.
it.wikipedia lists Pilzone as a frazione of Iseo (comune aggregated 1927); Brescia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia names Martignano as the frazione of Sulzano (Brescia).

it.wikipedia: Gerolanuova was a comune until 1928, Zurlengo was added to it 1816-1859 (its comune cited as Gerola con Zurlengo), both now in Pompiano (Brescia); point is Gerolanuova, Zurlengo is ~3.6 km away.
it.wikipedia says that in 1836 Terrasini was merged with the neighbouring village Favarotta; Palermo collections agree.
it.wikipedia says Valenzano is a nucleus within the territory of the old comune of Camignone (now a frazione of Passirano, Brescia).
it.wikipedia says La Comune di Castel Novo con Colorne e Onzato was the Napoleonic-era comune, renamed Castel Mella in 1864; Colorne and Onzato are its frazioni.
it.wikipedia lists Pontecasale (one word; spacing is typography) as a frazione of Candiana, Padova.
it.wikipedia says the autonomous comune of Favaro included Campalto, Tessera and Dese; Venezia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia describes the church of Santa Cristina as a dependency of the pieve of Quinto, and the area as Santa Cristina di Quinto di Treviso; Treviso collection agrees.
it.wikipedia (ghost-towns list) says Brancaleone (Superiore) in Reggio Calabria was moved to the coast, now Brancaleone; the point is the modern town, the old village lies a few km inland.
it.wikipedia: San Pietro Montagnone (San Pietro Montagnon in Veneto) became a comune in 1921 and was renamed Montegrotto Terme in 1934; Padova collection agrees.

it.wikipedia: the coast strip called Marina di Fiumedinisi kept that name until 1849, then became San Ferdinando and, in 1863, Nizza di Sicilia; Messina 1820-1865 agrees; register spelling has an extra n (Fiumendinisi), not independently attested.
Wikidata item Bovalino carries the alias Bovalino Marina and it.wikipedia distinguishes Bovalino Marina from Bovalino Superiore; Reggio Calabria collection agrees.
it.wikipedia (Rovolon) calls the 13th-century comune of the same place Rovolone; the name is not in Wikidata aliases, so this rests on that one article line and the Padova path.
it.wikipedia says Mira was formed in 1868 from the three comuni Gambarare, Mira and Oriago; Venezia collection agrees.
The only Meduna comune in Treviso province; Wikidata has the alias Meduna di Livenza and it.wikipedia lists frazioni such as Brische; Treviso collection agrees.

placed.n: Riva: Parrochia di Santa Maria Assunta
placed.why: it.wikipedia says Riva del Garda was formerly Riva and its parish church is Santa Maria Assunta in the archdiocese of Trento; Trento diocesan collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: Torriana was called Scorticata until 1938 and was a comune including the frazione Montebello (Rimini).
it.wikipedia: Paderno was a comune with its frazione Fietta until 2019; Treviso collection agrees.

it.wikipedia lists Matonti-Vetrali as a frazione of Laureana Cilento (Salerno) and Wikidata gives it a point; the Salerno civil-registration collection agrees; the bare name Matonti is taken as the first element of that frazione name.

placed.gazetteer: Episcopio (frazione of Sarno), drawn at Sarno
placed.why: it.wikipedia lists Episcopio as one of the two recognised frazioni of Sarno (Salerno), seat of the Sarno co-cathedral; the frazione has no own Wikidata coordinates, so the comune's P625 is used.

it.wikipedia: the comune of Zelarino (which also comprised the frazione Trivignano) was suppressed in 1926 and both are now in Venice's Chirignago-Zelarino municipality; Venezia 1806-1817 collection agrees.
it.wikipedia lists Croce among the frazioni of Musile di Piave (Venezia); the Napoleonic comune name joins Croce (di Piave) and Musile, both within the modern comune.

placed.n: Arco: Parrochia di Santa Maria Assunta
placed.why: it.wikipedia names the Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta in the centre of Arco; the diocese of Trento collection agrees.
it.wikipedia: Esenta is a frazione of Lonato del Garda and the Venzago territory (Castel Venzago, Centenaro, Madonna della Scoperta) was bought by Lonato in 1408/1416; Brescia collection agrees.
it.wikipedia infobox lists Malpaga, Mezzane and Viadana as frazioni of Calvisano (Brescia).
it.wikipedia infobox lists Carzago Riviera and Mocasina as frazioni of Calvagese della Riviera (Brescia); Wikidata alias Calvagese.

Quinzano d'Oglio is the only Quinzano comune in Brescia province and tuttitalia lists Cascina Castelletto places within it; WEAK: Mezzullo is not found in any page opened, so the Napoleonic combination is inferred from the head name.
it.wikipedia infobox lists Colombaro and Timoline (seat) as frazioni of Corte Franca (Brescia); the old comune is now inside it.

placed.n: Trento: Parrochia di Santa Maria Maggiore
placed.why: it.wikipedia on Trento names the church of Santa Maria Maggiore in the city; the Diocesi di Trento collection agrees.

placed.n: Trento: Parrochia di Santi Pietro e Paolo
placed.why: it.wikipedia on Trento lists the Chiesa dei Santi Pietro e Paolo (12th century, near Piazza dell'Anfiteatro); the Diocesi di Trento collection agrees.
it.wikipedia infobox lists Cesovo and Brozzo as frazioni of Marcheno (Brescia); Wikidata Brozzo is 'frazione in Marcheno'.
it.wikipedia lists Boldeniga, Corticelle Pieve and Quinzanello as frazioni of Dello (Brescia).
it.wikipedia: Leivi, in the Genova metropolitan city, was formerly called San Rufino until 1934; the Chiavari/Genova collection agrees.

it.wikipedia: Mola is a borgo of Formia, merged in 1820 with Castellone into the comune later renamed Formia (1862); en.wikipedia calls it Mola di Gaeta; Wikidata aliases of Formia include Mola; the Caserta 1809-1866 collection agrees. Point is Formia's (the borgo has no own coordinates).
it.wikipedia on Paratico lists Rivatica among the contrade of the comune (Brescia).
it.wikipedia infobox lists Ca' Rainati and Liedolo as frazioni of San Zenone degli Ezzelini (Treviso).

it.wikipedia: San Michele, formerly dependent on Latisana, became an autonomous comune in 1807 and was renamed San Michele al Tagliamento in 1867; the exact form 'di Latisana' is not printed there, so this rests on that history and the Venezia 1806-1817 collection.
it.wikipedia infobox lists Losson della Battaglia and Marteggia as frazioni of Meolo (Venezia).

Official name is San Vito sullo Ionio (Catanzaro); 'sull'Ionio' is the elided spelling of the same name; the Catanzaro collection agrees. No page opened prints the elided form, so this is a spelling-level inference.
it.wikipedia: the comune of Farra di Soligo was called Farra until 1867 and includes Soligo; the Treviso collection agrees.
Wikidata/it.wikipedia Valsanzibio is a settlement in Galzignano Terme (Padova); the spaced form differs only in spacing (typography); the Padova collection agrees.
it.wikipedia on Colle Umberto has a 'Frazioni e località' section with San Martino; the frazione has no own point found, so the comune's P625 is used.
it.wikipedia infobox lists Casella, Pagnano and Villa d'Asolo as frazioni of Asolo (Treviso).

placed.n: Ala: Parrochia di Santa Maria Assunta
placed.why: it.wikipedia: parish church of Santa Maria Assunta, patroness of Ala; the Diocesi di Trento collection agrees.
Wikidata Colbertaldo is a settlement in Vidor (Treviso).
it.wikipedia lists Poggiana, Spineda and Vallà as frazioni of Riese Pio X (Treviso); WEAK on 'Poiana', read as Poggiana, which the pages do not state.
it.wikipedia: the comune name was Mareno until 1867, now Mareno di Piave (Treviso).

it.wikipedia/Wikidata: Figline Valdarno was the comune (Firenze) before the 2014 merger; 'e frazioni' reads as the comune with its hamlets; Toscana collection agrees. Other Figline places (e.g. a frazione of Prato) are not comuni.

placed.n: Trento: Parrochia di Santa Maria Maddalena
placed.why: it.wikipedia on Trento: Contrada Santa Maria Maddalena named after the old, now vanished, church of Santa Maria Maddalena in the city; Diocesi di Trento collection agrees.

placed.gazetteer: San Pietro a Vico (frazione of Lucca)
placed.why: Wikidata item San Pietro a Vico is a settlement in Lucca (Q13373) with its own coordinates; the Lucca 1807-1814 collection agrees.
it.wikipedia on Cordignano lists Pinidello as a frazione and Silvella among its localities; Wikidata has both in Cordignano (Treviso).

refused.why: The name itself lists several Quebec counties (Island of Montreal, Laprairie, Chambly, Vaudreuil-Soulanges) in one filing label for the civil-copy church-record index, so it is not one place.
Indonesian for 'Application for a child's birth certificate'; the path level is [Record Type], so it names a kind of record, not a place.
The name itself says it is not one place ('Various towns').
The name says it is a list of foreign countries (paths: Philippines, Luzon, Cuba, etc.) for US 1900 census military, not one place.
The name itself says it is a combination of all localities, so it is not one place.
The name itself says it is not one place ('Statewide' across several states' naturalization collections).
The name itself says it is a unit, not a place.
The name itself says it is several towns (under various provinces), not one place.

refused.n: Gouvernment d'Aigle et du bailliage de Gessennay
refused.why: The name joins two separate Bernese jurisdictions, the governorate of Aigle (Vaud, Q43195) and the bailiwick of Gessenay (Saanen, Bern), roughly 60 km apart, so it is not one place.
'Varias provincias' means 'several provinces'; the name itself is not one place.
The name is the plural 'Villaggi' (it.wikipedia, Messina: the 48 casali around the city), i.e. several villages, not one place.
